verdict.rationale: Mem0's docs describe built-in Graph Memory on the Platform that automatically links people, places, and concepts across memories, with no external graph database, and position it for entity-centric questions. However, nothing documents multi-hop traversal, and the docs say the explicit relations field from earlier versions is gone, so how entities and relationships are exposed or queried is unclear. Missing for 10: evidence of multi-hop query answering, documentation of how entity/relationship structure is exposed or queried after the relations field was removed, confirmation of graph support in Open Source, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can store memories as a knowledge graph of entities and relationships so multi-hop and entity-centric questions are answerable

citations.quote: Mem0 Platform builds a native graph linking people, places, and concepts across your memories, with no external graph database to provision.
Graph Memory is built in. There is no Neo4j, Memgraph, or other graph store to deploy, no connection strings to manage, and nothing to enable.
Mem0 Platform automatically organizes your memories into a graph... without you defining any schema.
Mem0 now builds the graph itself from your memories.
